The expected number of distinct values after 100 seconds is 2025/101.

After 100 seconds, each position holds the maximum of the 201 consecutive original values centered at it. Call the window centered at i "window i". The number of distinct values is the number of distinct window maxima around the circle.

**Contiguity.** The windows whose maximum is a given value form a contiguous arc of the circle. So the number of distinct values equals the number of indices i where the maximum of window i differs from the maximum of window i+1. This also holds when all windows share one maximum, since 201 is much smaller than 2025.

**Probability of a change.** Window i is [i−100, i+100] and window i+1 is [i−99, i+101]. Their union has 202 elements. The two windows share the middle 200, and the exclusive elements are i−100 and i+101. The maxima differ exactly when the maximum of the union lies at one of these two exclusive positions. If the union's maximum is in the shared part, both windows have the same maximum. If it is at i−100, only window i contains it, and the maxima differ. The same holds for i+101 and window i+1. The values are i.i.d. continuous, so the maximum of the 202 elements is equally likely to be at any position. Hence

P(change at i) = 2/202 = 1/101.

**Expectation.** Summing over all 2025 indices by linearity of expectation gives

E = 2025/101.

ANSWER: 2025/101
